subject: SwiftCart throughput & tokenflow — post-demo follow-up and asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Pratt <sam.pratt@swiftcart.com>; Alex Nguyen <alex@swiftcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: SwiftCart throughput & tokenflow — post-demo follow-up and asks

Thanks for the demo today — appreciate the team walking us through the checkout assistant flow. Below is a concise recap and a few asks so we can size an initial pilot and provide a candidate configuration (latency SLOs + throughput headroom).

Call recap (short):
- Primary feature: multi-step checkout assistant (streaming responses back to the web client).
- Important SLOs: 95th perc latency target for first-stream-token ~200ms, end-to-end completion <1.2s for short prompts.
- Traffic shape you mentioned: steady baseline during business hours with short peak bursts around marketing campaigns.
- Auth/data: customer messages include order IDs/PG data (PII) — you requested on-prem or VPC options later in procurement.

Throughput / workload inputs we captured (please confirm):
- Typical concurrent sessions during baseline: ~120 active users (web sessions)
- Peak concurrent sessions during campaign crest: ~1,200 active sessions for ~3–5 minute window
- Average tokens per interaction: 180 tokens (prompt + context + expected completion)
- Expected QPS range: baseline ~8 QPS, peak burst ~80 QPS
- Tokens/sec (aggregate) baseline ~1,440 tokens/sec, peak ~14,400 tokens/sec (assuming average 180 tokens per request)

Clarifying asks / action items for sizing:
1) Can you confirm the average and 95th percentile tokens per request (we used 180 avg as above)? A small sample of production logs (anonymized) would be ideal — prod_traffic_sample.jsonl attached is a suggested format.
2) Do you require streaming partial token delivery to the browser (yes/no)? We want to ensure we size for streaming concurrency vs. batch generation.
3) Concurrency model: are multiple parallel outstanding requests per session common (e.g., user opens multiple chats)? Please give a rough multiplier (1x, 1.5x, 2x).
4) Latency tolerance per route (if you have separate SLOs for quick prompts vs. long-form completions).

What we’ll deliver after these clarifications:
- A one-page pilot sizing recommendation (GPU pool sizing, recommended batching/configs, and expected cost estimate for hosted vs. dedicated).
- A test plan and telemetry hooks we’ll use to validate the 95th latency and streaming throughput during the pilot.

Attachments: swiftcart_sample_prompts.txt (sample prompts + tokens estimate), prod_traffic_sample.jsonl (sample format), initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx (draft sizing)

Next steps: please reply with the prod sample and confirm streaming requirement. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30min follow-up tomorrow to go line-by-line.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Sam Pratt <sam.pratt@swiftcart.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@swiftcart.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 18:20:14 -0700
Subject: Re: SwiftCart throughput & tokenflow — post-demo follow-up and asks

Irene — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications and answers below.

- Tokens per request: our telemetry shows median ~160 tokens and 95p ~320 tokens across the past 30 days (we're including system prompts + user context).
- Streaming: yes, streaming partial tokens to the web client is required for the UX — we surface token-level output as it’s generated.
- Concurrency per session: typically 1 outstanding request per session, but during rapid flows (cart edits + suggestions) we see spikes where a session has up to 2 concurrent requests. Use 1.5x multiplier for safety.
- Latency: quick prompts (short suggestions) need the 95th ~200–250ms target; longer compositional responses can tolerate up to 1.5–2s.

Attached a redacted sample of production events (I removed order IDs) — link to S3 style export: https://s3.company/swiftcart/prod_sample_0902.jsonl (we'll also drop a copy in the Drive folder).

One more ask: can you provide a rough cost ballpark for a 30-day pilot (with the pilot including 4h/day of peak loads at the campaign level) so our finance lead can greenlight? If you can't give a firm price, a top-line estimate (hosted vs dedicated) is fine.

Thanks,
Sam Pratt
Product Lead, AI Assist
sam.pratt@swiftcart.com

Hi Sam — quick follow from infra/ops side after reviewing the sample and the numbers Irene captured. High level sizing guidance below; Marissa from infra here.

Assumptions we used for the draft sizing:
- 95p tokens/request 320 (per your telemetry)
- Effective avg tokens/request for resource planning: 220 (we account for distribution skew)
- Concurrency multiplier: 1.5
- Burst crest duration: ~5 minutes every campaign (you said short crests)

Pilot recommendation (initial):
- Hosted pilot: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a shared pool with streaming-optimized runtime, continuous batching tuned to keep first-token latency ~200–250ms. This covers baseline + 2x expected headroom for short bursts.
- Dedicated pilot: 2 x 8-GPU nodes (for predictability) if you want hard isolation; expect lower p95 latency variance and easier capacity planning.

Estimated throughput math (rough):
- Peak aggregate tokens/sec estimate (safety margin): 14,400 tokens/sec * 1.2 safety factor = ~17,300 tokens/sec
- With our runtime and optimizations, a single A100-equivalent GPU (streaming) can sustain ~2,500–3,500 tokens/sec for conversational models with prefix caching. We used 3,000 tokens/sec for quick planning.
- So 6 GPUs * 3,000 = 18,000 tokens/sec (covered).

Cost ballpark for a 30-day pilot (hosted, including telemetry retention and 24/7 support): ~$65k–$95k (depends on exact peak hours). Dedicated pilot monthly commit estimate: $80k–$120k (includes reserved capacity pricing and support). We'll produce a refined estimate once we have the exact peak-hour duration and traffic histogram.

Attachments: initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx (draft numbers + node config)

Next steps I propose:
1) Sam: drop the 72-hour raw traffic export (anonymized) or confirm the Drive link — we'll ingest and run a short load synthesis test.
2) We’ll run a quick internal throughput validation (bench) against your sample traffic shape and report back with tuned GPU count and expected p95 under streaming.
3) Schedule a 30-min sizing sync next Tue (Irene + Marissa + Ben + SwiftCart PMs) — propose Tue 09/07 @ 10am PT.

Ben — looping you for any cost/contract flags.

Marissa Cole
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
